_readme: Language-neutral pin for the daemon socket contract. Read by daemon/internal/protocol/corpus_test.go, daemon/internal/server/corpus_test.go and src/main/helper/daemon-protocol-corpus.test.ts. The TS and Go sides claim to mirror each other byte for byte; this file is what makes that claim fail loudly instead of drifting. Same arrangement as internal/guard/testdata/corpus. Edit a value here only when the wire contract really changes, and expect both suites to go red until both sides follow.
_ops: Every op the daemon serves. An op added to one side only fails the other side's test: Go checks each name dispatches to something other than `unknown op`, TS checks the DAEMON_OPS value matches exactly.
_lockFreeOps: Ops the server answers without taking the state mutex.
_windows: The Windows service's contract: the same framing over a named pipe, without OpenVPN or the IPsec probe, plus three read-only ops for facts the app reads for itself on Linux. Pinned by daemon/internal/protocol/corpus_test.go and daemon/internal/server's Windows tests.
_requests: Framing and parse taxonomy. `outcome` is one of valid | invalidJSON | invalidRequest | blank. The two invalid outcomes get a fixed {"id":0,...} reply and the connection STAYS OPEN — deviation 3 from the bash helper, because any group member could otherwise bounce the daemon with a single `null` line.
_responses: Exact bytes the daemon writes. Field ORDER is part of the contract as Go emits it (id, ok, result, error); result and error are omitted when empty.
_staleDaemonMarker: What an OLD daemon replies to an op it does not know. vpn-manager matches this prefix to detect a daemon left running across an upgrade; it is the fallback for daemons too old to answer protocol_version.
_limits: Values both sides enforce and must agree on: the split-tunnel cap (ops.MaxBypassRoutes / config-guard's sanitizeBypassRoutes) and the argv word that turns LAN sharing on (guard.LanSharingArg / LAN_SHARING_ARG). They were two hand-kept literals each.
_results: What the read-only ops answer with. server/corpus_test.go marshals the real producers and compares keys and JSON types; daemon-client's readers are tested against these and against malformed variants, which must read as 'cannot know'. traffic_counters, default_route and other_vpns are Windows-only; ops/results_shape_test.go pins their Go types on every platform.
